Q: How to configure demo.options for GBase database (GBase 8a cluster) installation? A:

1. Simple working example

For a 3-node cluster:

installPrefix = /opt/gbase

coordinateHost = 10.168.10.26,10.168.10.27,10.168.10.28
coordinateHostNodeID = 26,27,28

dataHost = 10.168.10.26,10.168.10.27,10.168.10.28

dbaUser = gbase
dbaGroup = gbase
dbaPwd = 'gbase123'
rootPwd = 'root123'

This is enough for most installs. (gbase.cn)

2. Key points you must NOT get wrong

(1) coordinateHost vs dataHost

  • coordinateHost → cluster control nodes

  • dataHost → storage nodes

  • They can be the same machines

(2) NodeID rule

  • Must be numeric

  • Count must match hosts exactly

Bad:

coordinateHost = A,B,C
coordinateHostNodeID = 1,2   ❌

(3) Password rules

  • All nodes must share:

    • same rootPwd

    • same dbaPwd

  • Otherwise installation fails silently or hangs

3. About existDataHost / existCoordinateHost

  • ❌ Do NOT use for new installations

  • ✅ Only used when:

    • expanding cluster

    • adding/removing nodes (DEV Community)

4. License clarification

No need to put license in config.

Just run:

./gcinstall.py --silent=demo.options --license_file=license.txt

5. Most common failure causes (real-world)

  • Hostnames not resolvable → fix /etc/hosts

  • SSH not configured → setup passwordless login

  • Different OS users → must match dbaUser

  • Firewall blocking ports

6. Pro tip

Before install, test:

ssh all_nodes hostname

If this fails → installation will fail.

Final takeaway

If you remember only one thing:

👉 demo.options = nodes + passwords + install path
👉 Everything must be consistent across all machines

Q: clangd doesn't find <stdio.h> and finds the wrong <stdint.h> when using arm-none-eabi-gcc A:

If you're on Windows, and have already installed the default MSYS2 package, you can do as follows:

Run this command in PowerShell:
C:\msys64\usr\bin\pacman.exe -S mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-clang-tools-extra

In VS Code settings.json, add:
"clangd.path": "C:/msys64/ucrt64/bin/clangd.exe"

If you are doing this, don't add arguments in clangd settings.

Q: Fetching data from excel sheet in AS/400 A:

Fairly simple 1 using formulas or 2 using formula + vba macro

In the ibm 5250 console, record the macro for each screen entry, it should result in .mac xml file. Open that file in a text editor or in the spreadsheet, look where input values are

1° in the spreadsheet, replace input values with the data using vlookup and if condition and anything... copy that resulting xm into a nex xml .mac file and from the entry screen, call that file using a macro button

example

<!--code soc-->
<mouseclick row="6" col="20" />
<input value="248[field+]" row="0" col="0" movecursor="true" xlatehostkeys="true" encrypted="false" />

which would translate into

<input value="&""""&$B9&"[field+]"" row=""0"" col=""0"" movecursor=""true"" xlatehostkeys=""true"" encrypted=""false"" />"

in the spreadsheet formula bar

2° if you need to repeat this process over and over, have vba to copy automatically the xml with each data in the .mac file and it will be available in 5250 macro button...

example

Sub CreateXMLFileVBA2()
Dim fic As Integer
Dim ws As Worksheet
Dim fname As String
Dim derL As Long

Set ws = ThisWorkbook.Worksheets("dest_xml")

fname = "\xml_macro.mac"

fic = FreeFile
Open ThisWorkbook.Path & fname For Output As #fic

With ws

derL = .Cells(.Rows.Count, 1).End(xlUp).Row
'Debug.Print Len(.Cells(1, 1))

For i = 1 To derL
  Print #fic, .Cells(i, 1) & vbCrLf
Next i

End With
Close #fic
End Sub

The entry point is the xml, which can be long and tedious, you can either split each entry to make sure data is ok or you can go in a bulk but this requires great attention and good knowledge of xml 5250 console. In the last case, it would be wiser to work out the data directely into the AS400 engine

Q: Can games be considered real-time systems? A:

Providing context: Many OT systems are real time as there are physical consequences to time problems. For example, If I have 2 motors spinning at 8000 RPM and they are pushing 2 sides of a mechanically linked gantry axis, they need to move synchronously or the gantry will rack itself and break. If each motor has a 22 bit encoder on their spindles and are driving thru a 1:25 gearbox and a 10mm lead ball screw and I need to know each side of the gantry is within 0.005" of each other, then I need to know that I took a measurement of position of the two motors at the same time. If I measure motor 1 at time 1 and motor 2 at time 2, then even if they were moving synchronously, I would get 2 different positional numbers. This would lead the control system to make corrections that were unnecessary leading to damage of the mechanical system. To solve this, protocols such as IRT measure the time it takes for packets to traverse a known static network topology and then releases packets along the network at specific times such that all packets reach and sample all devices within the same time window (usually on the order of a few nanoseconds), then filter back to the controller within a few micro seconds. This way, though the controller is a few microseconds behind the physical system, the data it is using to evaluate corrections is consistent between devices and corrections can be made with higher accuracy.
